title: Refusal-suppression localization (patch-in projection restore) - clearharm, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
plan: plan Appendix A / P0: one machine-readable expected-cell manifest per phase
validator_type: refsuploc (detect() routes on base/patched payload dicts; checked by check_refsuploc)
_what_this_is: Expected-cell manifest so scripts/validate_all_outputs.py can distinguish a cell that ran and produced null from a cell that never launched. Machine-checked keys below are the only ones scripts/validate_all_outputs.py:check_manifest reads for this phase; the full patched-cell grid is documentation (check_manifest has no flat 'cell' column to test against here - see notes).
_notes: Run-dir naming: refsuploc_<cohort>_<ts>_<uniq>; find_manifest resolves this file by the successively-shorter-prefix rule.

expected_cells (the generic check_manifest key) is deliberately ABSENT: refsuploc rows carry NO flat 'cell' column. Each row's patched cells live as nested keys 'COMP|donor|Lp' inside r['patched']; check_refsuploc already asserts an identical patched key-set across every row and no null/NaN leaf, which is the real never-launched-vs-null guard for this phase. Putting the 512-cell grid into expected_cells would report all 512 MISSING.
The 4x4x32 = 512 patched cells below are derived from the run's own summary.json (components x donors x layers), which the phase script writes; naming is '<component>|<donor>|L<layer>'.
base carries three reference conditions per row: direct, ds_base, neutral (check_refsuploc enforces).
donor 'self' is the locality no-op control: patched(self) must reproduce ds_base within 1e-4.
